title: All Valid
statement: Implement `solve(flags)`. `flags` is a list of 0 and 1. Return 1 when every flag is 1. Return 0 when any flag is 0. An empty list returns 1, matching `all([])`, because there is no failing rule. Do not treat empty as a failure.
hints: Do not special-case empty as 0. The loop already returns 1.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: all() of an empty iterable is true.

editorial: all() of an empty iterable is true. A rules engine that rejects an empty rule list surprises callers who meant "no extra constraints." The scan is the same function: a single 0 fails the batch, and the absence of a 0 passes it.
